1	"""Semi-vectorial finite-difference mode solver for strip/rib waveguides.
2	
3	This module solves the scalar-per-polarization ("semi-vectorial") wave
4	equation on the waveguide cross-section with finite differences, giving
5	SiPhon an in-library reference against which its own effective index
6	method (:class:`siphon.waveguide.Waveguide`) can be checked.
7	
8	Physics
9	-------
10	For the quasi-TE mode (dominant electric field component Ex, parallel to
11	the wafer plane) the semi-vectorial equation is
12	
13	    d/dx [ (1/eps) d(eps Ex)/dx ] + d^2 Ex / dy^2 + k0^2 eps Ex = beta^2 Ex
14	
15	with eps = n(x, y)^2, k0 = 2 pi / wavelength, and n_eff = beta / k0. The
16	first term enforces continuity of the normal displacement eps*Ex across
17	vertical (x-normal) interfaces — the Stern (1988) scheme — while Ex and
18	dEx/dy stay continuous across horizontal interfaces. Quasi-TM (dominant
19	Ey) is the same with x and y roles swapped. Polarization coupling is
20	neglected entirely: each mode is a single field component.
21	
22	Discretization: nodes at the centers of uniform rectangular cells. The
23	grid is uniform per axis: the x pitch is dx_um snapped *down* so that
24	x = +/- width/2 falls exactly on cell boundaries, and the y pitch
25	targets dx_um / 4 (snapped down so y = 0 and y = height fall on cell
26	boundaries). The finer y pitch is deliberate: the vertical direction
27	carries the fastest field variation (thin, high-index-contrast core
28	layer), and its measured O(h^2) error constant is ~5x the horizontal
29	one, so a quarter-pitch y grid balances the two error contributions at
30	modest extra cost. Aligning interfaces to cell boundaries removes the
31	first-order n_eff jitter that node/interface misalignment otherwise
32	causes. Permittivity is area-averaged over each cell (only rib slab
33	interfaces can then straddle a cell), interface continuity is built into
34	the off-diagonal coefficients by harmonic (1/eps) averaging between
35	neighbouring cells, and the boundary condition is Dirichlet (field = 0)
36	at the edge of the padded window. The sparse eigenproblem is solved by
37	shift-invert Arnoldi (:func:`scipy.sparse.linalg.eigs`) around
38	beta^2 = k0^2 n_core^2, i.e. just above the largest possible guided-mode
39	eigenvalue, so the largest-n_eff modes converge first.
40	
41	Honesty limits
42	--------------
43	Budgeting-to-design grade, not signoff. Expect roughly 1e-3 absolute
44	n_eff accuracy for well-guided modes at the default dx = 0.02 um; weakly
45	guided modes near cutoff and quasi-TM modes with strong corner fields are
46	less accurate. There is no polarization coupling (no hybrid modes, no
47	TE/TM anti-crossings), no PML (leaky/radiating modes are truncated by the
48	Dirichlet wall), and no loss. Use a full-vectorial solver for final
49	signoff.
50	
51	Conventions: wavelengths and dimensions in um; quasi-TE means dominant
52	E-field parallel to the wafer plane. Field arrays are indexed
53	``field[j, i]`` at ``(x_um[i], y_um[j])`` with y = 0 at the bottom of the
54	core (top of the buried oxide).
55	"""
56	
57	from __future__ import annotations
58	
59	from dataclasses import dataclass
60	
61	import numpy as np
62	import scipy.sparse as sp
63	import scipy.sparse.linalg as spla
64	
65	from . import materials
66	
67	
68	@dataclass(frozen=True, eq=False)
69	class FdMode:
70	    """One guided mode from the finite-difference solver.
71	
72	    Attributes
73	    ----------
74	    neff : effective index beta / k0 (dimensionless).
75	    polarization : 'TE' (dominant Ex) or 'TM' (dominant Ey).
76	    field : real 2D array, shape (len(y_um), len(x_um)); the dominant
77	        transverse E component sampled at (x_um[i], y_um[j]) as
78	        ``field[j, i]``, normalized so max |field| = 1 (arbitrary units —
79	        the semi-vectorial solve carries no absolute power scale).
80	    x_um, y_um : 1D grid coordinates in um. x = 0 is the horizontal
81	        center of the core; y = 0 is the bottom of the core.
82	    """
83	
84	    neff: float
85	    polarization: str
86	    field: np.ndarray
87	    x_um: np.ndarray
88	    y_um: np.ndarray
89	
90	
91	def _cell_fraction(centers: np.ndarray, half: float, lo: float, hi: float) -> np.ndarray:
92	    """Fraction of each cell [c-half, c+half] that lies inside [lo, hi]."""
93	    a = centers - half
94	    b = centers + half
95	    return np.clip((np.minimum(b, hi) - np.maximum(a, lo)) / (b - a), 0.0, 1.0)
96	
97	
98	def _epsilon_map(
99	    x: np.ndarray,
100	    y: np.ndarray,
101	    dx: float,
102	    dy: float,
103	    width_um: float,
104	    height_um: float,
105	    slab_um: float,
106	    eps_core: float,
107	    eps_clad: float,
108	    eps_box: float,
109	) -> np.ndarray:
110	    """Cell-averaged permittivity eps(x, y) = n^2, shape (ny, nx).
111	
112	    Geometry: buried oxide for y < 0; core rectangle |x| <= width/2,
113	    0 <= y <= height; for a rib, a residual core slab 0 <= y <= slab_um at
114	    all x; cladding everywhere else. Each grid cell gets the area-weighted
115	    average of eps over the cell. With the snapped grid the core outline
116	    coincides with cell boundaries, so only rib slab interfaces are ever
117	    averaged.
118	    """
119	    fx_core = _cell_fraction(x, dx / 2.0, -width_um / 2.0, width_um / 2.0)  # (nx,)
120	    fy_core = _cell_fraction(y, dy / 2.0, 0.0, height_um)  # (ny,)
121	    fy_slab = (
122	        _cell_fraction(y, dy / 2.0, 0.0, slab_um) if slab_um > 0 else np.zeros_like(y)
123	    )
124	    fy_box = _cell_fraction(y, dy / 2.0, -1e9, 0.0)  # (ny,)
125	
126	    f_core = np.outer(fy_core, fx_core) + np.outer(fy_slab, 1.0 - fx_core)
127	    f_box = np.broadcast_to(fy_box[:, None], (y.size, x.size))
128	    f_clad = 1.0 - f_core - f_box
129	    return f_core * eps_core + f_box * eps_box + f_clad * eps_clad
130	
131	
132	def _assemble(
133	    eps: np.ndarray, dx: float, dy: float, k0: float, polarization: str
134	) -> sp.coo_matrix:
135	    """Assemble the semi-vectorial operator A with A e = beta^2 e.
136	
137	    Stern coefficients: along the polarization direction (x for TE, y for
138	    TM) the term d/du [(1/eps) d(eps E)/du] is discretized in flux form
139	    with u = eps E continuous and flux v = (1/eps) du/du continuous, so
140	    the cell-boundary coefficient is the harmonic mean of 1/eps, i.e.
141	    2 / (eps_0 + eps_p). Coupling from node 0 to neighbour p is then
142	    2 eps_p / (eps_0 + eps_p) / h^2 with matching diagonal term
143	    -2 eps_0 / (eps_0 + eps_p) / h^2 (Stern 1988). The other direction is
144	    the plain second difference. Dirichlet boundaries: edge nodes simply
145	    lack the outside neighbour (field 0 there).
146	    """
147	    ny, nx = eps.shape
148	    n = ny * nx
149	    dx2 = dx * dx
150	    dy2 = dy * dy
151	
152	    epad = np.pad(eps, 1, mode="edge")
153	    e0 = eps
154	    e_e = epad[1:-1, 2:]  # east  (x + dx)
155	    e_w = epad[1:-1, :-2]  # west  (x - dx)
156	    e_n = epad[2:, 1:-1]  # north (y + dy)
157	    e_s = epad[:-2, 1:-1]  # south (y - dy)
158	
159	    if polarization == "TE":  # dominant Ex: Stern averaging along x
160	        c_e = 2.0 * e_e / (e0 + e_e) / dx2
161	        c_w = 2.0 * e_w / (e0 + e_w) / dx2
162	        c_n = np.full_like(e0, 1.0 / dy2)
163	        c_s = np.full_like(e0, 1.0 / dy2)
164	        diag = (
165	            -(2.0 * e0 / (e0 + e_e) + 2.0 * e0 / (e0 + e_w)) / dx2
166	            - 2.0 / dy2
167	            + k0 * k0 * e0
168	        )
169	    else:  # TM, dominant Ey: Stern averaging along y
170	        c_n = 2.0 * e_n / (e0 + e_n) / dy2
171	        c_s = 2.0 * e_s / (e0 + e_s) / dy2
172	        c_e = np.full_like(e0, 1.0 / dx2)
173	        c_w = np.full_like(e0, 1.0 / dx2)
174	        diag = (
175	            -(2.0 * e0 / (e0 + e_n) + 2.0 * e0 / (e0 + e_s)) / dy2
176	            - 2.0 / dx2
177	            + k0 * k0 * e0
178	        )
179	
180	    idx = np.arange(n).reshape(ny, nx)
181	    rows = np.concatenate(
182	        [
183	            idx.ravel(),
184	            idx[:, :-1].ravel(),  # -> east neighbour exists
185	            idx[:, 1:].ravel(),  # -> west neighbour exists
186	            idx[:-1, :].ravel(),  # -> north neighbour exists
187	            idx[1:, :].ravel(),  # -> south neighbour exists
188	        ]
189	    )
190	    cols = np.concatenate(
191	        [
192	            idx.ravel(),
193	            idx[:, 1:].ravel(),
194	            idx[:, :-1].ravel(),
195	            idx[1:, :].ravel(),
196	            idx[:-1, :].ravel(),
197	        ]
198	    )
199	    vals = np.concatenate(
200	        [
201	            diag.ravel(),
202	            c_e[:, :-1].ravel(),
203	            c_w[:, 1:].ravel(),
204	            c_n[:-1, :].ravel(),
205	            c_s[1:, :].ravel(),
206	        ]
207	    )
208	    return sp.coo_matrix((vals, (rows, cols)), shape=(n, n))
209	
210	
211	def solve_modes(
212	    width_um: float,
213	    height_um: float,
214	    wl_um: float,
215	    *,
216	    slab_um: float = 0.0,
217	    core: str = "si",
218	    cladding: str = "sio2",
219	    box: str = "sio2",
220	    polarization: str = "TE",
221	    n_modes: int = 2,
222	    dx_um: float = 0.02,
223	    pad_um: float = 1.5,
224	) -> list[FdMode]:
225	    """Solve for guided quasi-TE or quasi-TM modes of a strip/rib waveguide.
226	
227	    Semi-vectorial finite differences on a rectangular grid, uniform per
228	    axis: x pitch ~dx_um and y pitch ~dx_um/4 (each snapped down so the
229	    core outline lies on cell boundaries; see module docstring for why y
230	    is meshed finer), over a window extending at least pad_um beyond the
231	    core on all four sides, with field = 0 (Dirichlet) at the window
232	    edge. See the module docstring for the discretized equation and its
233	    limits.
234	
235	    Parameters
236	    ----------
237	    width_um, height_um : core cross-section in um.
238	    wl_um : vacuum wavelength in um.
239	    slab_um : residual slab thickness in um for a rib; 0 for a strip.
240	    core, cladding, box : material names for :mod:`siphon.materials`
241	        (cladding = top/side, box = buried oxide below the core).
242	    polarization : 'TE' (dominant Ex) or 'TM' (dominant Ey).
243	    n_modes : maximum number of guided modes to return.
244	    dx_um : requested horizontal grid pitch in um. The actual x pitch is
245	        dx_um snapped down so width/2 is an integer number of cells; the
246	        y pitch is dx_um/4 snapped down so height is an integer number
247	        of cells. Default 0.02 gives roughly 1e-3 n_eff accuracy for
248	        well-guided SOI modes; halve it for a convergence check rather
249	        than trusting one grid.
250	    pad_um : cladding/box padding around the core in um. Must comfortably
251	        exceed the evanescent decay length of the slowest-decaying mode
252	        (1.5 um is ample for well-guided SOI modes at 1.55 um).
253	
254	    Returns
255	    -------
256	    list[FdMode]
257	        Guided modes with max(n_cladding, n_box) < n_eff < n_core, sorted
258	        by decreasing n_eff, at most n_modes long. May be shorter (or
259	        empty) if the structure guides fewer modes.
260	
261	    Raises
262	    ------
263	    ValueError
264	        On non-physical geometry, bad polarization, non-positive grid
265	        parameters, or a core index not above both claddings.
266	    """
267	    if width_um <= 0 or height_um <= 0:
268	        raise ValueError("width_um and height_um must be positive")
269	    if not 0 <= slab_um < height_um:
270	        raise ValueError("slab_um must satisfy 0 <= slab_um < height_um")
271	    if dx_um <= 0 or pad_um <= 0:
272	        raise ValueError("dx_um and pad_um must be positive")
273	    if n_modes < 1:
274	        raise ValueError("n_modes must be >= 1")
275	    pol = polarization.upper()
276	    if pol not in ("TE", "TM"):
277	        raise ValueError(f"polarization must be 'TE' or 'TM', got {polarization!r}")
278	
279	    n_core = float(materials.index(core, wl_um))
280	    n_clad = float(materials.index(cladding, wl_um))
281	    n_box = float(materials.index(box, wl_um))
282	    if n_core <= max(n_clad, n_box):
283	        raise ValueError("core index must exceed cladding and box indices")
284	
285	    k0 = 2.0 * np.pi / wl_um
286	
287	    # Snap pitches *down* (ceil on the cell count) so the core outline
288	    # lands exactly on cell boundaries, then put nodes at cell centers.
289	    # y is meshed at a quarter of dx_um: the vertical error constant is
290	    # ~5x the horizontal one (see module docstring). The x grid is
291	    # mirror-symmetric about x = 0, so mode symmetry is exact on the grid.
292	    dx = (width_um / 2.0) / max(1, int(np.ceil(width_um / 2.0 / dx_um)))
293	    dy = height_um / max(1, int(np.ceil(4.0 * height_um / dx_um)))
294	    mx = int(round(width_um / 2.0 / dx)) + int(np.ceil(pad_um / dx))
295	    x = (np.arange(2 * mx) - mx + 0.5) * dx
296	    my_lo = int(np.ceil(pad_um / dy))
297	    my_hi = int(round(height_um / dy)) + int(np.ceil(pad_um / dy))
298	    y = (np.arange(my_lo + my_hi) - my_lo + 0.5) * dy
299	
300	    eps = _epsilon_map(
301	        x, y, dx, dy, width_um, height_um, slab_um, n_core**2, n_clad**2, n_box**2
302	    )
303	    a = _assemble(eps, dx, dy, k0, pol).tocsc()
304	
305	    # Shift-invert just below the theoretical eigenvalue ceiling
306	    # beta^2 = k0^2 n_core^2: the nearest eigenvalues are the
307	    # largest-n_eff (best guided) modes.
308	    sigma = (k0 * n_core) ** 2 * (1.0 - 1e-6)
309	    k_req = min(max(n_modes + 2, 4), a.shape[0] - 2)
310	    vals, vecs = spla.eigs(a, k=k_req, sigma=sigma, which="LM")
311	
312	    n_min = max(n_clad, n_box)
313	    modes: list[FdMode] = []
314	    order = np.argsort(-vals.real)
315	    for m in order:
316	        beta2 = float(vals[m].real)
317	        if beta2 <= 0.0:
318	            continue
319	        neff = float(np.sqrt(beta2) / k0)
320	        if not (n_min < neff < n_core):
321	            continue
322	        v = vecs[:, m]
323	        peak = v[np.argmax(np.abs(v))]
324	        field = (v / peak).real.reshape(y.size, x.size)
325	        modes.append(FdMode(neff=neff, polarization=pol, field=field, x_um=x, y_um=y))
326	        if len(modes) == n_modes:
327	            break
328	    return modes
329

1	"""Tests for siphon.fdmode: semi-vectorial finite-difference mode solver.
2	
3	Physics anchors, all independent of the solver's own output:
4	
5	- Wide-strip limit: a 6.0 x 0.22 um strip approaches the analytic
6	  three-layer slab TE0 index (2.848 at 1.55 um) from
7	  :func:`siphon.waveguide.slab_neffs` (exact transcendental solve).
8	- Grid convergence: n_eff is O(h^2); halving the pitch must move it by
9	  well under the accuracy claim.
10	- Bounds and ordering: every guided n_eff lies strictly between the
11	  cladding and core material indices, and mode order is by decreasing
12	  n_eff.
13	- EIM cross-check ("the punchline"): the FD solver exists so SiPhon can
14	  bound its own EIM bias in-library; for the standard 500 x 220 nm strip
15	  the two must agree to well under a percent but must NOT agree exactly.

1	"""Waveguide mode solvers.
2	
3	Two levels of model, both fast and dependency-free:
4	
5	1. ``slab_neffs`` — exact transcendental solution of the three-layer slab
6	   waveguide (TE and TM), the workhorse of quick photonic reasoning.
7	2. ``Waveguide`` — strip/rib waveguide solved with the effective index
8	   method (EIM): vertical slab first, then the horizontal problem with the
9	   swapped polarization. Accurate to roughly the percent level for n_eff of
10	   well-guided modes; use a full vectorial solver for final signoff.
11	
12	Near modal cutoff the EIM is biased *conservative* (it declares modes guided
13	earlier than a full-vectorial solver: e.g. TE1 first appears at ~316 nm strip
14	width under EIM versus ~450-500 nm full-vectorial). When a solved mode sits
15	within ``NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN`` of the lateral cladding index the solver
16	emits an :class:`EimAccuracyWarning` rather than silently returning a number
17	that a vectorial solver might not reproduce. Architecture-level, not signoff.
18	
19	Conventions: wavelengths and dimensions in um; quasi-TE means dominant
20	E-field parallel to the wafer plane.
21	"""
22	
23	from __future__ import annotations
24	
25	import warnings
26	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
27	from functools import lru_cache
28	
29	import numpy as np
30	from scipy.optimize import brentq
31	
32	from . import materials

34	
35	class EimAccuracyWarning(UserWarning):
36	    """Warns that an EIM result is in the regime where the method is least accurate.
37	
38	    Emitted when the horizontally-solved effective index sits within
39	    ``NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN`` of the side/cladding effective index, i.e. the
40	    mode is marginally guided. Near cutoff the EIM is biased early/conservative
41	    (it guides modes a full-vectorial solver would find cut off), so the
42	    returned n_eff — and the mode's very existence — should be confirmed with a
43	    full-vectorial solver. The numerical result is returned unchanged.
44	    """
45	
46	
47	#: Margin (dimensionless, in effective-index units) below which a mode counts
48	#: as marginally guided: when the horizontally-solved n_eff sits within this of
49	#: the side/cladding effective index, the mode is barely confined laterally —
50	#: exactly where the EIM is least trustworthy and biased early/conservative
51	#: (validated example: TE1 first guided at ~316 nm strip width under EIM versus
52	#: ~450-500 nm full-vectorial). Crossing it triggers :class:`EimAccuracyWarning`.
53	NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN = 5e-3
54

56	def _slab_dispersion(neff, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness, m, polarization):
57	    """Zero of this function <=> guided slab mode m at n_eff = neff."""
58	    kappa = k0 * np.sqrt(n_core**2 - neff**2)
59	    gamma = k0 * np.sqrt(max(neff**2 - n_top**2, 0.0))
60	    delta = k0 * np.sqrt(max(neff**2 - n_bot**2, 0.0))
61	    if polarization == "TE":
62	        phi_top = np.arctan2(gamma, kappa)
63	        phi_bot = np.arctan2(delta, kappa)
64	    elif polarization == "TM":
65	        phi_top = np.arctan2((n_core / n_top) ** 2 * gamma, kappa)
66	        phi_bot = np.arctan2((n_core / n_bot) ** 2 * delta, kappa)
67	    else:
68	        raise ValueError("polarization must be 'TE' or 'TM'")
69	    return kappa * thickness - phi_top - phi_bot - m * np.pi
70	
71	
72	def slab_neffs(
73	    n_core: float,
74	    n_top: float,
75	    n_bot: float,
76	    thickness_um: float,
77	    wavelength_um: float,
78	    polarization: str = "TE",
79	    max_modes: int = 16,
80	) -> list[float]:
81	    """Effective indices of all guided modes of a three-layer slab.
82	
83	    Returns a list sorted from fundamental (highest n_eff) down; empty list
84	    if the slab guides no mode at this wavelength/polarization. Index
85	    contrasts below the ~2e-9 root-bracketing epsilon are numerically
86	    degenerate and report no modes (real platforms sit >= 1e-3 above it).
87	    """
88	    if thickness_um <= 0:
89	        return []
90	    if n_core <= max(n_top, n_bot):
91	        return []
92	    k0 = 2.0 * np.pi / wavelength_um
93	    n_min = max(n_top, n_bot)
94	    eps = 1e-9
95	    lo, hi = n_min + eps, n_core - eps
96	    if lo >= hi:  # contrast below bracketing epsilon: degenerate, no solve
97	        return []
98	    out: list[float] = []
99	    for m in range(max_modes):
100	        f_lo = _slab_dispersion(lo, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization)
101	        f_hi = _slab_dispersion(hi, k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization)
102	        if f_lo <= 0.0:
103	            break  # this and all higher-order modes are cut off
104	        if f_hi >= 0.0:  # numerically degenerate bracket; shouldn't happen
105	            break
106	        neff = brentq(
107	            _slab_dispersion,
108	            lo,
109	            hi,
110	            args=(k0, n_core, n_top, n_bot, thickness_um, m, polarization),
111	            xtol=1e-12,
112	        )
113	        out.append(float(neff))
114	    return out

118	class Waveguide:
119	    """Strip or rib waveguide on SOI (or SiN) solved by the effective index method.
120	
121	    Parameters
122	    ----------
123	    width_um, height_um : core cross-section.
124	    slab_um : residual slab thickness for a rib; 0 for a fully etched strip.
125	    core, cladding, box : material names understood by :mod:`siphon.materials`.
126	        ``cladding`` is the top/side cladding, ``box`` the buried oxide.
127	    """
128	
129	    width_um: float
130	    height_um: float
131	    slab_um: float = 0.0
132	    core: str = "si"
133	    cladding: str = "sio2"
134	    box: str = "sio2"
135	
136	    def __post_init__(self):
137	        if self.width_um <= 0 or self.height_um <= 0:
138	            raise ValueError("width_um and height_um must be positive")
139	        if not 0 <= self.slab_um < self.height_um:
140	            raise ValueError("slab_um must satisfy 0 <= slab_um < height_um")
141	
142	    # --- effective index -------------------------------------------------
143	
144	    def neff(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE") -> float:
145	        """Effective index of the fundamental quasi-TE or quasi-TM mode.
146	
147	        Raises ValueError if the structure guides no such mode.
148	
149	        If the mode is marginally guided (n_eff within
150	        ``NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN`` of the lateral cladding/slab effective
151	        index), an :class:`EimAccuracyWarning` is issued — the EIM is biased
152	        conservative near cutoff and the result should be checked with a
153	        full-vectorial solver. Because results are memoized (``lru_cache``),
154	        the warning fires only on the *first* computation for a given
155	        (geometry, wavelength, mode); repeated calls return the cached value
156	        silently.
157	        """
158	        return self._neff_cached(round(float(wavelength_um), 9), mode)
159	
160	    @lru_cache(maxsize=4096)
161	    def _neff_cached(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str) -> float:
162	        if mode.upper() not in ("TE", "TM"):
163	            raise ValueError(f"mode must be 'TE' or 'TM', got {mode!r}")
164	        n_core = materials.index(self.core, wavelength_um)
165	        n_clad = materials.index(self.cladding, wavelength_um)
166	        n_box = materials.index(self.box, wavelength_um)
167	
168	        # EIM polarization bookkeeping: quasi-TE of the channel guide uses the
169	        # TE slab solution vertically, then TM horizontally (and vice versa).
170	        vert_pol = "TE" if mode.upper() == "TE" else "TM"
171	        horiz_pol = "TM" if mode.upper() == "TE" else "TE"
172	
173	        core_slab = slab_neffs(n_core, n_clad, n_box, self.height_um, wavelength_um, vert_pol)
174	        if not core_slab:
175	            raise ValueError(
176	                f"no vertical slab mode for {self!r} at {wavelength_um} um ({mode})"
177	            )
178	        n_center = core_slab[0]
179	
180	        if self.slab_um > 0:
181	            side_slab = slab_neffs(
182	                n_core, n_clad, n_box, self.slab_um, wavelength_um, vert_pol
183	            )
184	            n_side = side_slab[0] if side_slab else max(n_clad, n_box)
185	        else:
186	            n_side = n_clad
187	
188	        if n_center <= n_side:
189	            raise ValueError(f"no lateral confinement for {self!r} ({mode})")
190	        horiz = slab_neffs(n_center, n_side, n_side, self.width_um, wavelength_um, horiz_pol)
191	        if not horiz:
192	            raise ValueError(f"no guided mode for {self!r} at {wavelength_um} um ({mode})")
193	        margin = horiz[0] - n_side
194	        if margin < NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN:
195	            warnings.warn(
196	                f"{self!r}: quasi-{mode.upper()} mode at {wavelength_um} um is "
197	                f"marginally guided (n_eff - n_side = {margin:.2e} < "
198	                f"{NEAR_CUTOFF_NEFF_MARGIN:.0e}). The EIM is biased "
199	                "early/conservative near cutoff; confirm this mode with a "
200	                "full-vectorial solver before relying on it.",
201	                EimAccuracyWarning,
202	                stacklevel=3,
203	            )
204	        return horiz[0]
205	
206	    # --- dispersion ------------------------------------------------------
207	
208	    def group_index(self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE", dwl_um: float = 1e-4) -> float:
209	        """Group index n_g = n_eff - lambda d(n_eff)/d(lambda).
210	
211	        Includes both waveguide and material dispersion (materials are
212	        re-evaluated at each finite-difference point).
213	        """
214	        n0 = self.neff(wavelength_um, mode)
215	        n_p = self.neff(wavelength_um + dwl_um, mode)
216	        n_m = self.neff(wavelength_um - dwl_um, mode)
217	        dn_dwl = (n_p - n_m) / (2.0 * dwl_um)
218	        return float(n0 - wavelength_um * dn_dwl)

220	    def dispersion_ps_nm_km(
221	        self, wavelength_um: float, mode: str = "TE", dwl_um: float = 5e-4
222	    ) -> float:
223	        """Chromatic dispersion parameter D = -(lambda/c) d^2 n_eff / d lambda^2.
224	
225	        Returned in the conventional units of ps/(nm*km).
226	        """
227	        n_p = self.neff(wavelength_um + dwl_um, mode)
228	        n_0 = self.neff(wavelength_um, mode)
229	        n_m = self.neff(wavelength_um - dwl_um, mode)
230	        d2n = (n_p - 2.0 * n_0 + n_m) / dwl_um**2  # 1/um^2
231	        c_um_per_ps = 2.99792458e2  # speed of light in um/ps
232	        d_ps_per_um2 = -(wavelength_um / c_um_per_ps) * d2n  # ps/um^2
233	        # convert ps per (um of bandwidth) per (um of length) -> ps/(nm*km)
234	        return float(d_ps_per_um2 * 1e-3 * 1e9)
